name: Neurosolv
description: An anti-neuroinflammatory compound formulated specifically for BCI-associated cerebral edema and glial scarring. Extended BCI use — particularly high-bandwidth sessions, combat BCI engagement, or jacked-in work shifts exceeding eight hours — causes measurable neuroinflammation around interface nodes and along data-pathway corridors in the brain. Neurosolv reduces this through selective COX-3 analog inhibition and targeted microglial suppression.
effects: decreases glial scar formation around interface nodes
alleviates BCI headache and pressure sensation
slows long-term neural degradation from heavy BCI use
side_effects: reduced BCI signal clarity while active — some users experience 'lag' sensation
rare: paradoxical increase in interface sensitivity causing sensory flooding
cultural_context: Anyone who jacks in hard knows the headache — the pressure behind the eyes after a long BCI session, the feeling that your skull is a size too small. Neurosolv is the aspirin of the augmented age. Data workers take it daily. Tier 1 hackers cut it with cheaper anti-inflammatories that don't cross the blood-brain barrier as cleanly. The long-term neural degradation from skipping it is well documented and largely ignored by people who have more immediate problems.
story_hooks: A data-entry worker in Tier 2 is developing early-stage interface node scarring because her employer's mandatory overtime bans Neurosolv use during shifts — the company claims it reduces productivity metrics — and she's trying to build a case before the damage becomes permanent.
The Shelf version of Neurosolv is being cut with a compound that actually accelerates glial scarring over time while reducing short-term symptoms — someone is profiting from the long-term damage.
A character discovers that their neuroinflammation isn't from BCI overuse — something in their implants is deliberately triggering it, and Neurosolv is just masking the symptom.
